newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly Speaker proposes NYC debt authority.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly Speaker proposes NYC debt authority.

text.p: New York State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver on Thursday, countering a proposal recently presented by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, proposed the creation of an emergency bonding authority for New York City that could sell up to $7.5 billion of bonds for capital projects through the year 2000.
Silver, a Democrat, also proposed a new method for calculating the city's debt sale limits. This proposal would be presented to voters as a constituional amendment.

Silver's proposal came in response to Mayor Giuliani's call for the creation of a city Infrastructure Finance Authority to address the city's current debt-cap crisis that could halt the city's borrowing program in 1997.
Silver said he was concerned about the mayor's authority, saying the mayor is "asking for a $10 billion blank check."
Silver's proposed authority would be temporary and would be controlled by the city until the state constitution is amended to allow for a new method of determining the city's debt limits.

The authority would be overseen by a five-member board consisting of the director of the city's Office of Management and Budget, the city finance commissioner, the city comptroller, one mayoral appointee and one appointed by the speaker of the City Council.
